To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chlorination of type III groundwater in the water supply systems of Hanoi, a city with more than 2 million inhabitants in Vietnam, results in a low efficiency for inactivation of Giarda lamblia cyst, and the formation of THMs, which is not in compliance with WHO and EU standards, and the formation is dominated by the formation of chloro-THMs.

(I) the THM formation in Hanoi's water supply system is mainly governed by the presence and concentration of bromide in the water and (II) the chlorination practice is not sufficient for inactivation of Giarda cysts in the water with high ammonia and arsenic levels.

the THMs formed from the chlorination of Hanoi's drinking water are below the WHO, EU, or US standards, the THMs are mainly chloroform and bromodichloromethane, the bromoforms are more important in high bromide water, the formation of THMs in high bromide and ammonia water is limited, the disinfection of high ammonia and arsenic contaminated water is not sufficient, and N-nitrosamines are not formed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the occurrence, fate, and control of THM in the drinking water of Hanoi City.
the occurrence, the fate and the speciation of THMs in the water supply of Hanoi City.
the formation of THMs in the chlorination of groundwater in water supplies in Vietnam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
type I water is not suitable for chlorination, type II water is suitable with a slight concern, and type III water is not suitable.
the chlorination practice in Hanoi water supply systems is sufficient to provide drinking water that is microbiologically safe.
the water supply system is not in a good condition, especially with regard to the high arsenic levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current chloramination of the type III water is not sufficient for the disinfection of protozoan pathogens and the removal of arsenic and ammonia.
the chlorination efficiency is sufficient for the disinfection of type I and II water, while type III water requires further improvement in the treatment process.
the chlorination efficiency is sufficient in type I and II water but not in type III water and that the THMs in the water supply are within the WHO guideline value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current chloramination practice is not sufficient to inactivate Giardia cysts in the type III groundwater of Hanoi City.
THM speciation is a useful indicator of the water quality of groundwater sources and that the formation of bromo-TRMs can still be expected even when bromide concentrations are low.
the chlorination of type III groundwater in Hanoi is not satisfactory in terms of disinfection efficiency, THM formation, and arsenic removal.
